note: What a server sends to say what led to a death, so the client can lay it out. The header names the unit this is about.

revisions.note: A client ignores the whole message where killer is zero. Each entry's size after source follows from event alone.

fields.name: killer
fields.note: The unit credited with the death. A client ignores the whole message where this is zero.

fields.name: span
fields.note: The time the entries below cover, in seconds.

fields.name: sourceType
fields.note: What sort of source the killer was. A client acts on it only where it holds killer.

bits.name: type
bits.note: Read as signed, -8 to 7. What each value means is not recorded for this range.

bits.name: unused
bits.note: A client reads nothing here; a server sends zero.

fields.name: blobLength
fields.note: How many bytes the entries below take together. A client reads no entries where this is zero or, read as signed, less.

fields.name: entryCount
fields.note: How many entries follow.

fields.name: entries
fields.note: What happened to the unit before it died, packed one after another.

items.name: entry
items.note: One thing that happened to the unit before it died. What follows source depends on event alone.

fields.name: time
fields.note: When it happened, in match seconds.

fields.name: count
fields.note: How many times.

fields.name: event
fields.note: What sort of thing, from 0 to 98, and so which fields follow: 10 and 11 are damage, 36 and 37 healing, 38 an effect. What the other values mean is not recorded for this range, nor what a client does with a value above 98.

fields.name: source
fields.note: The unit that did it. A client takes it as the attacker where the entry names no object it holds.

fields.name: target
fields.note: The unit it was done to.

fields.name: damage
fields.note: What damage of this sort carries.

fields.name: parent
